//: Hand-written starter questions (ADR 0010). Imported at start-up by key; edits made in /admin are kept. Little picture questions are live with word cards until they have pictures (2026-11-26). Facts were checked on 2026-11-26.

questions.prompt: Which animal says moo?
questions.explain: Cows say moo. I say moo when I'm sad. Different reasons.

questions.prompt: Which animal says quack?
questions.explain: Ducks quack. They also bite. Ask me how I know.

questions.prompt: What color is a banana?
questions.explain: Yellow! Unless you leave it on the counter for a week. Then it's brown and sad.

questions.prompt: Which one can fly?
questions.explain: Birds fly. Fish swim. Dogs nap. I relate to the dog.

questions.prompt: Which shape is round?
questions.explain: A circle! Round and round and round. Like this game.

questions.prompt: Which animal lives in the water?
questions.explain: Fish live in the water. So did I, back when I had a ship.

questions.prompt: Which one is hot?
questions.explain: The sun is super hot. Don't touch it. Seriously.

questions.prompt: Which one is a fruit?
questions.explain: An apple! Please don't eat the shoe.

questions.prompt: How many days are in a week?
questions.explain: Seven. Five of them are Monday, emotionally.

questions.prompt: What do bees make?
questions.explain: Honey! Bees work all summer for it, then we steal it. Pirate move, honestly.

questions.prompt: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explain: Earth. Last I checked. I'll check again later.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest animal that has ever lived?
questions.explain: The blue whale. Bigger than any dinosaur. Its heart is the size of a small car.

questions.prompt: What color do you get when you mix blue and yellow?
questions.explain: Green! Like my face after I lose. Which is every round.

questions.prompt: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.explain: Eight. Eight legs. All of them running toward me.

questions.prompt: True or false: a tomato is a fruit.
questions.explain: True! It grows from a flower and has seeds. Ketchup is basically jam. Fight me.

questions.prompt: What does a caterpillar turn into?
questions.explain: A butterfly! It goes into a cocoon a little worm and comes out fancy. Inspiring.

questions.prompt: How many points does a snowflake usually have?
questions.explain: Six, because of the way water freezes. No two exactly alike. Like my excuses.

questions.prompt: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explain: The Pacific. I sailed it once. Well, a bit of it. The bit near the dock.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of France?
questions.explain: Paris. I'm banned from two of its cafés.

questions.prompt: How many continents are there?
questions.explain: Seven, the way most schools count them. Some countries count six. Nobody counts eight. Nobody.

questions.prompt: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.explain: Mars. It's red because of rusty dust. Same as my old ship.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in from the air to make food?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide. They breathe in what we breathe out. Teamwork.

questions.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explain: Leonardo da Vinci. Took him years. I can't finish a sandwich.

questions.prompt: What is the hardest natural material?
questions.explain: Diamond. Second hardest: this question, apparently.

questions.prompt: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.explain: Six. Bees build with them. Bees are smarter than me.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest mountain above sea level?
questions.explain: Everest, about 8,849 meters. I get winded on stairs.

questions.prompt: Before pumpkins, what did people in Ireland carve for Halloween?
questions.explain: Turnips! Smaller, harder and much creepier. Pumpkins were a big upgrade.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explain: Au, from the Latin aurum. Ag is silver. I had both once. Briefly.

questions.prompt: In which year did people first walk on the Moon?
questions.explain: 1969, Apollo 11. They had less computing power than your phone. Your phone uses it for this.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell is called its powerhouse?
questions.explain: The mitochondria. The one fact everyone remembers from biology.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.explain: Two. The only even prime. One doesn't count. One never counts.

questions.prompt: Which country has the most people?
questions.explain: India. It passed China around 2023, by the UN's count.

questions.prompt: Which animal has fingerprints so like ours that they could confuse a crime scene?
questions.explain: The koala! Even under a microscope they're hard to tell apart. Koalas: suspects.

questions.prompt: Which element has the atomic number 1?
questions.explain: Hydrogen. Simplest atom there is. Relatable.

questions.prompt: What is the longest river in Africa?
questions.explain: The Nile. Some say longest in the world; the Amazon fans disagree. Loudly.

questions.prompt: How many bones are in an adult human body?
questions.explain: 206. Babies have more; some fuse as you grow. Mine mostly ache.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest building in the world?
questions.explain: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, about 828 meters. For now: Jeddah Tower is being built to beat it.

questions.prompt: True or false: lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.explain: False. The Empire State Building gets hit about 20 times a year. Lightning holds grudges.

questions.prompt: Besides lime, what is the main ingredient in a classic margarita?
questions.explain: Tequila. Ask me how many I've had tonight. Actually, don't.
